reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) Press Release
reports.description: Sierra Leone's national CPI. Stats SL's November 2025 press release states: "We are using the Modified Laspeyres formula to compute indices according to the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) with 12 functions," base "December 2021=100." A June 2026 release (14.77% YoY inflation) confirms ongoing monthly publication. MODERATE CONFIDENCE: Stats SL's own site returned a bot-detection captcha wall on two direct fetch attempts, so this quote is AI-summarized (WebFetch) rather than independently pdftotext-verified — treat as plausible, not verbatim-confirmed, pending a future direct extraction.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, per Stats SL's own press release series; confirmed current through June 2026 per the CPI index page.

reports.title: Local Government Act, 2004 (No. 1)
reports.description:
UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.20, municipal-tier round 25): This Act is now legally SUPERSEDED by The Local Government Act, 2022 (see sl-local-government-act-2022 in af-sierra-leone-municipal.json), whose own preamble states its purpose is "to repeal and replace the Local Government Act 2004." The 2022 Act carries forward and extends the financing framework described below (its own Sections 49-53), including an explicit grant-adequacy floor (S.53) not present in the 2004 text. Retained below for historical reference and because the 2004 Act's own text remains independently useful evidence of Sierra Leone's earlier fiscal-decentralization framework.

Sierra Leone's (former, 2004-2022) Local Government Act. Verified directly via downloaded PDF + pdftotext extraction. Part VII (Financial Matters): S.45(1) "Local councils shall be financed from their own revenue collections, from central government grants for devolved functions and from transfers for services delegated from Government Ministries"; S.46(1) tied annual grants for devolved functions and administrative costs; S.58 "Revenue raised from local taxes and from mining revenues, other than those collected by the Government, shall be shared between the local councils and the Chiefdom Councils"; S.60 mining-revenue share for local councils "as may be determined by the Ministry." STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: Sierra Leone's four "provinces" (Northern, North West, Southern, Eastern) plus Western Area are purely administrative groupings with no elected government or budget of their own — actual fiscal transfers under this Act flow to the district/city council and Chiefdom Council tier, not to a provincial-level entity. This national law is nonetheless the correct instrument for this corpus's provincial/state tier, since no separate provincial fiscal law exists to find.

_dropped.why: Sierra Leone's own National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (NSDS) 2016-2020 names ECOWAS once, but only in connection with a proposed regional TRAINING initiative ("NSS will explore with ECOWAS the scope for a regional wide training initiative"), not CPI methodology — does not satisfy a CPI-specific citation, so not minted as an edge. AFRISTAT, WAMA/AMAO, Mano River Union, the African Charter on Statistics, and SHaSA were all searched for in the NSDS and NOT found. Separately, ECOWAS's own regional statistical-harmonisation guidelines (Industrial Production Index, Business Register, Government Financial Transactions/TOFE-ECOWAS, Quarterly National Accounts) explicitly EXCLUDE CPI from their scope and do not name Sierra Leone specifically.
